title: The unstruck sound at the heart
hookLine: headphones build quiet out of sound; the old map finds it at the heart
carry: anahata: the sound heard within that nothing strikes
tomorrow: the Goddess has a thousand names. two of them are addresses.

cards: Noise-canceling headphones make quiet out of sound: they listen to the room and play back its opposite. Silence, built by a machine working hard. The old chakra map keeps a stranger kind of quiet near its center.
It names the lotus at the heart for a sound that nothing strikes. So, one question for today: where does real quiet come from?

teach.b: The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana describes the lotus at the heart and explains its name, Anahata: here, it says, the unstruck sound is heard. Every other sound has a cause you could find, a stick, a string, a voice.
This one is pictured as heard in deep meditation, not made.

teach.h: NADA: THE DIVINE KNOWN AS SOUND.
teach.b: Behind it sits a big Hindu teaching: nada, sound, is one of the ways the divine is known. That's why OM is chanted before prayers, and why the yoga texts teach listening inward until the mind grows still in the sound.
So the quiet at the heart isn't produced by effort. It's found. Now a neighbor.
In the Hebrew Bible, the prophet Elijah, worn out and hiding in a cave, is told to stand on the mountain before the Lord. A great wind tears at the rocks, but the Lord is not in the wind.
Then an earthquake, then a fire, and the Lord is in neither.

The King James Version gives the next words: "and after the fire a still small voice." Jews and Christians both read that scene, and here two traditions look for the holy in quiet rather than in force.
That's what they share. Here's the honest difference.

teach.h: A VOICE THAT SPEAKS; A SOUND WITHIN.
teach.b: Elijah's voice speaks to him: God addressing a prophet, with words and a task.
The unstruck sound is heard within, on a map of the body, and says nothing in words. Two quiets, each in its own house.

how: In meditation on the heart center, some practitioners rest attention at the chest and listen inwardly, as the texts describe the unstruck sound; many begin by chanting OM. It is usually learned with a teacher.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: a love charm worn close to the heart
a map whose heart is a quiet that nothing strikes
a chart of the heart's beats and rhythms

p: the wind, the earthquake, the fire
the Lord was not in them

s: Hindu traditions treat sound itself as a way the divine is known
it's called nada; it's why OM is chanted and why yoga texts teach listening inward.
the still small voice and the unstruck sound are the same idea in two languages
both look for the holy in quiet; Elijah's voice speaks to him, while anahata is heard within, without words.
the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana explains the heart lotus's name by the unstruck sound
the text gives its own reason for the name: the sound with no striker is heard there.

games.q: a friend's yoga teacher says the 'heart chakra' is about loving people more. by the old map, what's the heart lotus named for?
o: a sound heard within in meditation, one that nothing strikes.
romantic love and being kind to everyone.
the heartbeat you can hear with a stethoscope.
games.why: the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana names it Anahata, unstruck, for the sound heard there in meditation. kindness is good; it just isn't what the name means.

practice: If you know OM, chant it once, slowly, and listen to the silence after it for the rest of the sit. If you don't chant, choose one quiet sound near you, a fan, your own breath, and listen for the quiet underneath it.
There's nothing to make here, only something to hear.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: at its heart, Anahata, named for a sound heard in meditation that nothing strikes.

orig.note: Sanskrit: unstruck; the name of the heart lotus, for the sound heard there.

carryVoice: Your line: anahata, the sound heard within that nothing strikes. Quiet, not force. Rest well tonight.

sources.ref: Sat-Cakra-Nirupana, on the heart lotus (called Anahata because the unstruck sound, anahata-shabda, is heard there)
Hatha Yoga Pradipika, chapter 4 (nadanusandhana: listening inwardly to the inner sound until the mind is absorbed)

sources.q: and after the fire a still small voice.
